items.stem: If sec θ − tan θ = m, then the value of sec θ + tan θ is
items.answer: Use the identity sec²θ − tan²θ = 1. Factorising the left side, (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = 1, so sec θ + tan θ = 1/(sec θ − tan θ) = 1/m.

If θ is an acute angle of a right angled triangle, then which of the following equation is not true ?

options.label: A
options.text: sin θ cot θ = cos θ

options.label: B
options.text: cos θ tan θ = sin θ

items.answer: For an acute angle θ, tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ, so sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 and therefore tan²θ − sec²θ = −1, not 1. The other three statements are standard and true, so option (d) is the one that is not true.

items.stem: cos²θ/sin²θ − 1/sin²θ, in simplified form is :
items.answer: cos²θ/sin²θ − 1/sin²θ = cot²θ − cosec²θ. Since cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ, this equals cot²θ − 1 − cot²θ = −1.

items.stem: If sin θ − cos θ = 0, then the value of (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ) is
items.answer: sin θ − cos θ = 0 gives sin θ = cos θ = sin(90° − θ), so θ = 90° − θ and θ = 45°. Then sin⁴ 45° + cos⁴ 45° = (1/√2)⁴ + (1/√2)⁴ = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.

items.stem: If sin A = 1/2, then the value of cot A is
items.answer: sin A = perpendicular/hypotenuse = 1/2, so taking perpendicular 1 and hypotenuse 2, the base is √(2² − 1²) = √3. Then cot A = base/perpendicular = √3/1 = √3.

items.stem: The value of the expression cosec(75° + θ) − sec(15° − θ) − tan(55° + θ) + cot(35° − θ) is
items.answer: Rewrite the first and last terms with complementary angles: cosec(75° + θ) = cosec[90° − (15° − θ)] = sec(15° − θ), and cot(35° − θ) = cot[90° − (55° + θ)] = tan(55° + θ). The expression becomes sec(15° − θ) − sec(15° − θ) − tan(55° + θ) + tan(55° + θ) = 0.

items.stem: If sin θ = a/b, then cos θ is equal to
items.answer: sin θ = a/b = perpendicular/hypotenuse, so the base is √(b² − a²). Hence cos θ = base/hypotenuse = √(b² − a²)/b.

items.stem: If cos(α + β) = 0, then sin(α − β) can be reduced to
items.answer: cos(α + β) = 0 = cos 90°, so α + β = 90° and α = 90° − β. Then sin(α − β) = sin(90° − β − β) = sin(90° − 2β) = cos 2β.

items.stem: If cos 9α = sin α and 9α < 90°, then the value of tan 5α is
items.answer: cos 9α = sin α means sin(90° − 9α) = sin α, so 90° − 9α = α and 10α = 90°, giving α = 9°. Then tan 5α = tan 45° = 1.

items.stem: If △ABC is right angled at C, then the value of cos(A + B) is
items.answer: In △ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. Since ∠C = 90°, A + B = 90°. Hence cos(A + B) = cos 90° = 0.

If 4 tan θ = 3, then ((4 sin θ − cos θ)/(4 sin θ + cos θ)) is equal to
items.answer: From 4 tan θ = 3, tan θ = 3/4. Dividing numerator and denominator by cos θ gives (4 tan θ − 1)/(4 tan θ + 1) = (4(3/4) − 1)/(4(3/4) + 1) = (3 − 1)/(3 + 1) = 2/4 = 1/2.

items.stem: If x = p sec θ and y = q tan θ, then
items.answer: Since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, substitute sec θ = x/p and tan θ = y/q to get (x/p)² − (y/q)² = 1. Multiplying through by p²q² gives x²q² − y²p² = p²q².

items.stem: If b tan θ = a, the value of (a sin θ − b cos θ)/(a sin θ + b cos θ) is
items.answer: From b tan θ = a, tan θ = a/b. Divide numerator and denominator by cos θ: (a tan θ − b)/(a tan θ + b) = (a(a/b) − b)/(a(a/b) + b) = (a² − b²)/(a² + b²).

items.stem: (cos⁴A − sin⁴A) is equal to
items.answer: cos⁴A − sin⁴A = (cos²A)² − (sin²A)² = (cos²A − sin²A)(cos²A + sin²A) = (cos²A − sin²A)(1) = cos²A − (1 − cos²A) = 2 cos²A − 1.

items.stem: If sec 5A = cosec(A + 30°), where 5A is an acute angle, then the value of A is
items.answer: cosec(A + 30°) = sec[90° − (A + 30°)] = sec(60° − A). So sec 5A = sec(60° − A), giving 5A = 60° − A. Then 6A = 60° and A = 10°.
items.ocr: The printed solution writes the complementary step as sec[90° − (A − 30°)], a typo for sec[90° − (A + 30°)]; its own next line, sec(60° − A), and the key (d) 10° are both correct, so nothing is contradicted.

items.stem: If x sin³θ + y cos³θ = sin θ cos θ and x sin θ = y cos θ, than x² + y² is equal to
items.answer: Write the first equation as (x sin θ) sin²θ + (y cos θ) cos²θ = sin θ cos θ. Using x sin θ = y cos θ, this is x sin θ(sin²θ + cos²θ) = sin θ cos θ, so x sin θ = sin θ cos θ and x = cos θ. Then x sin θ = y cos θ gives cos θ sin θ = y cos θ, so y = sin θ. Hence x² + y² = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.

If tan θ + sin θ = m and tan θ − sin θ = n, then m² − n² is equal to
items.answer: m² − n² = (tan θ + sin θ)² − (tan θ − sin θ)² = 4 tan θ sin θ = 4√(tan²θ sin²θ). Now tan²θ sin²θ = sin²θ(1 − cos²θ)/cos²θ = tan²θ − sin²θ = (tan θ + sin θ)(tan θ − sin θ) = mn, so the value is 4√(mn).

items.stem: If f(x) = cos²x + sec²x, then f(x)
items.answer: f(x) = cos²x + sec²x = cos²x + sec²x − 2 + 2 = cos²x + sec²x − 2 cos x · sec x + 2, since cos x · sec x = 1. This is (cos x − sec x)² + 2, and a square is never negative, so f(x) ≥ 2.

items.answer: From the identity cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1, factorising gives (cosec θ + cot θ)(cosec θ − cot θ) = 1, so cosec θ − cot θ = 1/(cosec θ + cot θ) and the assertion is true. The reason is the very identity used to prove it, so it is true and is the correct explanation of the assertion.

items.answer: sin θ = perpendicular/hypotenuse, so sin θ = 4/3 would need a perpendicular of 4 against a hypotenuse of 3. The hypotenuse is the largest side of a right triangle, so the perpendicular can never exceed it and this value is impossible. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

items.answer: cot 80° = cot(90° − 10°) = tan 10°, so sec²10° − cot²80° = sec²10° − tan²10° = 1 and the assertion is true. It is also true that sin 30° = 1/2, so the reason is true. But sin 30° plays no part in proving the assertion, so the reason is not its correct explanation.
